$comment: Schema for /qa-test's summary.json (reports/tickets/{SPRINT}/<ticket-key>/summary.json). The ONLY narrative-adjacent artifact /qa-test persists (per .claude/rules/reports.md §1) — it must carry every field a later consumer needs: 1b's cross-sprint duplicate check reads `date`; 5e's Feature Release Gate reads `regression`; 5g records `promotion`; 5f records `layer` + `release`, whose only reader is /ba-analyze docs release. Replace <..> placeholders; 0/[]/null are empty defaults.

timing.$comment: Wall-clock for THIS /qa-test run. Per-suite durations are a different record and already live in reports/regression/history.json (durationField() in scripts/lib/regression-triage.ts derives them from the runner envelope) — do not duplicate them here. This block exists because the 40-minute regression window and the FAST/FULL split are both claims about cost, and before it the schema carried 78 keys and not one duration, so neither claim could be checked. regression_predicted_minutes is the makespan `regression:select --target` predicted; regression_actual_minutes is what the run took. An order-of-magnitude gap between them is the known ×18-×88 estimatedMinutes defect surfacing (see scripts/lib/suite-selection.ts) — record it, don't reconcile it away.

build.$comment: THREE version facts, not one, because they answer different questions and disagreeing on them produces the two worst QA outcomes available: filing a bug against a feature that was never deployed, and signing off a fix that never landed. `platform`/`theme`/`relevant_modules` are the DECLARED state (vc-deploy-dev backend/packages.json — git). `deployed` is what GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/modules actually reports — the ground truth, and routinely different (deploy in flight, failed, partially applied). A failed probe records the string UNKNOWN and NEVER falls back to declared. Full precedence rule: .claude/templates/agent-dispatch.md § Build Verification.

deployed.$comment: Probed, not read from git. UNKNOWN is a legal value; an absent/guessed value is not.

releasedThrough.$comment: Written by 1b item 2a from .claude/knowledge/domain/release-ledger.md. `ledger_generated` is that file's own `generated:` date — the run's freshness bound (stale after 45 days). `behind[]` lists components where deployed < released, i.e. shipped upstream but not testable here: those are NOT_DEPLOYED, never FAIL. `breaking[]` lists ⚠ BREAKING rows in the component(s) under test — a non-empty array is a FAST->FULL forcing condition (see 1b item 2a), so recording it is what makes that routing decision re-derivable afterwards. Empty arrays are the normal, correct state on a quiet month; null means the ledger was not consulted, which is a gap, not a zero.

release.$comment: Written at 5f for a PASS/PASS_WITH_NOTES verdict — the MACHINE half of the per-ticket release-note fragment. The prose half is ba-doc-writer's reports/ba/release-notes/<ticket>-<layer>-release-note.md, and this block is the ONLY thing that doc may take a layer, a version or a breaking flag from (ba-doc-writer never re-derives them; a second derivation site is how the two drift). It exists because the top-level `layer` is the axis a release note routes on (layer -> audience -> skeleton, .claude/knowledge/ba/virto-doc-style.md §9) and nothing here recorded it: `regression.suites` carries the layer of what was RE-TESTED, `build` carries versions of what was DEPLOYED, and neither answers 'which surface did THIS ticket change'. A null block means the release step never ran (FAIL/BLOCKED, or a run predating the block) — a gap, not 'nothing shipped'. `fragment` null WITH a non-null `refusal` is the opposite: the step ran and declined, and the reason is the finding. `component_versions`/`platform_version` are copied from build.deployed (PROBED) — never from build.relevant_modules (declared git state) and never from release-ledger.md, which records what shipped UPSTREAM, not what is deployed here; UNKNOWN is legal, an absent or guessed version refuses the fragment. `breaking` is true only from build.releasedThrough.breaking[] or a cited contract change in the diff — never from ticket, PR or commit prose, so breaking:true with breaking_source:null is a defect in the fragment.

epic.$comment: parent = the Epic this story belongs to (null if none). roll_up is written only on an --epic serial run (in the Epic's own summary), combining the child-story verdicts + the cross-story E2E into one Epic recommendation.

ac_dod_estimate.$comment: Filled by 5b. ac_coverage_pct = conditions_with_evidence/conditions_total. dod_* are null/0 when the ticket states no DoD (1e DoD field = 'none stated').

iterations.$comment: Only when invoked with --iterate (Step 5k — .claude/skills/qa-test/modes.md). `rounds` = how many test(->fix->re-test) rounds ran (the initial run IS round 1); `outcome` = how the loop ended. `per_round` is the record 5k step 4 demands in prose — 'a per-round summary (what each round fixed, what still fails)' — and previously had nowhere to live: every other field in this file is single-valued, so round 2 overwrote round 1's verdict, counts, regression run_id and timing, and the cap-reached hand-off cited per-round numbers no artifact could support. INVARIANT: per_round.length === rounds and per_round[i].round === i+1. WRITTEN AT THE END OF EVERY ROUND, not at loop exit — the loop can STOP at any round (G0 BAIL, BLOCKED, the cap, a dropped session), and a history persisted only on a clean exit is missing exactly when it is needed. `enabled: true` with an empty per_round is a contradiction, not a default: it means the run claimed the loop and recorded no round.

per_round.$comment: One entry per round. WHAT THE SINGLE-VALUED TOP-LEVEL FIELDS MEAN ONCE THERE ARE N ROUNDS: `verdict`, `total_cases`/`passed`/`failed`/`blocked`, `regression.*`, `regression_triage.*` and `promotion` are the LATEST round's — the build a human is being asked to ship — NOT the best and NOT the first. `bugs_filed`, `bugs_not_filed` and `new_cases_authored` are CUMULATIVE across rounds (a round-1 Sub-task must not vanish from the artifact because round 2 filed nothing). `timing` is the WHOLE run: started_at = round 1's start, finished_at = the last round's finish, steps.step4/steps.step5 summed across rounds. Round 1's own numbers survive ONLY here — never reconstruct them from the top level.

build.$comment: What this round ACTUALLY tested, probed from GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/modules — never assumed from the deploy PR, because /qa-deploy-pr --verify is advisory by its own contract. The loop's whole claim is that the code changed between rounds; unprobed, a 'still failing' round is indistinguishable from a deploy that never landed. UNKNOWN is legal; a guess is not. `deploy_pr` is the /qa-deploy-pr deploy PR (round >=2 only; null on round 1). `deploy_confirmed` records the mandatory human confirm before that deploy — false on round 1, and false at round >=2 means the loop deployed without asking, which is a defect in the run.

red_green.$comment: The re-run of exactly the previously-FAILED cases, as its OWN /qa-regression run (--ids), kept out of the Artifact-C run so its pass rate answers one question and the release gate's >=95% keeps answering another. Round 1: all null/empty — there is no previously-failed set yet, and that is not a gap. FAST: run_id stays null and `checklist_items` carries the re-run items instead of `cases`, because a FAST round re-runs failed checklist items through one agent and produces no RUN_ID.

regression.$comment: This round's change-scoped Artifact-C run, RE-SCOPED to the fix's diff (regression:select --repo <name> --diff <fix-PR range>), never reused from round 1 — round 1's scope came from the ticket's diff and cannot know what the fix touched. A non-null skipped_reason means the gate cannot be evaluated on this round.

bugs_carried.$comment: A bug THIS RUN filed in an earlier round that is still failing. Neither re-filed nor relabelled PRE-EXISTING: it keeps its original IN-SCOPE provenance and severity (so it still fails 5c this round) and gets one comment on its existing Sub-task. Re-filing would produce N tickets for one defect; PRE-EXISTING would stop it failing the ticket that caused it.

bugs_fixed.$comment: A bug filed in an earlier round whose case(s) went GREEN in this round. Commented on its own Sub-task and recorded here, deliberately NOT transitioned: TESTED is the furthest /qa-test may move anything and Done/Cancelled are forbidden, and the fix is an UNMERGED prerelease, so nothing has shipped. The human who merges closes it.

qa_fix.$comment: One /qa-fix invocation per in-scope fixable bug this round. outcome pr-open = G0-G7 cleared and a PR is open (never merged); bail = a G0 BAIL, which STOPs the loop and hands THAT bug to a human. An empty array on a FAIL round means no in-scope fixable bug remained and the loop fell back to the pointer close-out — a legitimate ending, and one the loop-level `outcome` alone cannot express.

artifacts.$comment: What this round changed in the durable artifacts, so a diff is attributable to a round rather than to 'the run'. `model_amendment` = a `## Round N` section appended to the ONE Step-1e model file (never a second dated file — a same-day round 2 collides on <TICKET>-<date>.md, and two files split one fault model in two). `cases_authored` = cases authored FROM a loop-confirmed defect, the strongest `plausible:` ground the KEEP gate accepts; they must be authored BEFORE the round that re-runs them or they execute nowhere and 5g holds them at Draft with PR-002. `checklist_section` names the appended section — the checklist is append-only because the RED->GREEN transition is the loop's deliverable.

still_failing: <one line per condition/case still red at the end of this round>

promotion.$comment: Filled by 5g (runs last, non-blocking). Cases are appended to regression/suites/ as Draft in Step 3; after Step 4's automated regression run 5g flips each promotable case Draft→Automated (green under the automated runner) or Draft→Reviewed/Manual (checklist-only), reverts non-promotable rows, and leaves a case that failed on a real in-scope bug at Draft with a reason.

blocked.reason: unresolved {HYPOTHESIS} — <what stayed unknown> | failed on in-scope bug <link>

regression.$comment: The change-scoped Artifact-C /qa-regression run — the Feature Release Gate (5e) is defined on THIS run_id, not whole-history. On an --iterate run this is the FINAL round's Artifact-C run — the one the gate is computed on; earlier rounds' runs are in iterations.per_round[].regression.

regression_triage.$comment: Filled by 5a item 0 when Artifact C produced a RUN_ID. invoked = whether /qa-triage-results <run_id> --fix ran; the three arrays mirror its triage-report.md tables (confirmed bugs / test-case fixes applied / dismissed).

bugs_filed.$comment: One entry per confirmed bug filed at 5d. `severity` is recorded so the 5d severity floor is auditable from this artifact rather than only from the comment. On an --iterate run this array is CUMULATIVE across rounds; the round that filed each entry is in iterations.per_round[].bugs_filed.

bugs_not_filed.$comment: One entry per confirmed real bug held BELOW the 5d severity floor (Low/P3). Present and empty when there are none — an absent array is indistinguishable from a run that found none. `report` is the durable record; the floor drops a finding from the tracker, never from the run.
